children: USA Rare Earth, Pasqal and Riven Systems are teaming up to develop separation technology for rare earth production.

The companies said Thursday the project aims to identify new separation molecules that bind more effectively to rare earths than current alternatives, allowing for smaller, lower-cost and less energy-intensive processing facilities.

Under the project, Riven--which specializes in artificial intelligence for industrial chemistry--would conduct automated experiments and generate the data needed to build machine learning models of extractant selectivity for rare earth elements. French quantum computing company Pasqal would then use a quantum processing unit to benchmark quantum machine learning models against classical computing-based models to help USA Rare Earth optimize extractant selection, the companies said.

The project aims to counter a key challenge facing the rare earth industry outside of Asia: separating mixed rare earth carbonate produced in upstream operations into individual, separated oxides, said Alex Moyes, senior vice president of upstream USA at USA Rare Earth.

"The Chinese dominate this capability, especially for vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium, terbium and yttrium. Our goal is to accelerate the path to efficient, competitive and sustainable solutions by changing how the rare earth industry discovers the chemistry it runs on, replacing years of trial-and-error," Moyes said.

The companies said they expect the initial machine learning project could create opportunities for a deeper, extended collaboration. Over time, the companies envision an end-to-end extractant discovery process where a quantum machine learning model identifies high-potential extractants, those extractants are tested in Riven's self-driving lab and top candidates are validated in USA Rare Earth's research and development facility.
